title: Poster stamp for the Cologne exhibition, 1907
lede: Joseph Maria Olbrich’s advertising stamp puts a tower in a diamond of laurel, and fits the exhibition text into ruled bands of squared capitals.
summary: A laurel diamond over stacked, ruled bands of tightly packed capitals, in one gray ink. Joseph Maria Olbrich, 1907.

source.label: MAK Collection Online: Werbemarke zur Kölner Ausstellung 1907, KI 21484-3-311

evidence.note: Downloaded and inspected the MAK photograph of the stamp MAK KI 21484-3-311 (1198 × 1680 px). The photograph is soft and shows JPEG blocking, so fine details of the laurel and the tower figure are uncertain.

styles.note: Clear for the lettering and layout: symmetrical, framed, with capitals packed into ruled bands. It is a German commission by one of the founders of the Secession.

context: The MAK records the object as a poster stamp (Werbemarke) designed by Joseph Maria Olbrich in 1907, printed in collotype, 4.5 × 3.1 cm. The text reads “Mai / Kölner / October / Ausstellung / veranstaltet v. d. A. G. Flora / Kunst und Kunstgewerbe / wechselnde Ausstellungen”. It is part of an album of poster stamps from the Werner J. Schweiger collection. [MAK KI 21484-3-311](https://sammlung.mak.at/en/collect/werbemarke-zur-koelner-ausstellung-1907_276583).

Olbrich (1867–1908) was one of the founders of the Vienna Secession. [Wikipedia: Joseph Maria Olbrich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Maria_Olbrich). He completed the Secession building in 1898. [Wikipedia: Secession Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secession_Building).
observed: The stamp is printed in one dark gray ink on pale paper, with perforated edges.
A border of small scallops and dots frames the upper field.
A diamond (a square set on its point) made of dense laurel leaves holds a tall tower with a figure on top, on the central axis.
Below, the text sits in five ruled bands. “KÖLNER” and “AUSSTELLUNG” are large; smaller capitals in the lower bands fill each band from edge to edge.
“MAI” and “OCTOBER” sit in small boxes at the two ends of the “KÖLNER” band. The small words “v. d. A. G.” and “und” are set at a smaller size between larger words.
The capitals are narrow and geometric; the U is drawn as a V.
interpretation: Olbrich uses the same devices as the Vienna posters: a frame, a central emblem, and text blocks in which letter size and width change so that every line is full. The laurel echoes the laurel dome of his Secession building.
Because it is a single-colour miniature, the stamp shows how much of the style is carried by structure and lettering alone.
borrow: Give a small badge or card a central emblem in a square set on its point, with the text in full-width ruled bands below it.
Set small connecting words (and, of, from) in a much smaller size between large words, so the line stays justified.

images.alt: Gray perforated poster stamp: a diamond of laurel leaves around a tower, above ruled bands of capitals reading Mai, Kölner, October, Ausstellung, veranstaltet v. d. A. G. Flora, Kunst und Kunstgewerbe, wechselnde Ausstellungen.

rights.statement: The MAK marks this image with the [Public Domain Mark 1.0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Joseph Maria Olbrich died in 1908, and the stamp was issued in 1907, so the work is in the public domain in Germany, Austria, and the United States.
